title: Intelligent Invoice Processing
summary: An automated invoice-ingestion workflow that extracts structured invoice data from email and documents while explicitly handling duplicates, incomplete fields, non-invoices, unreadable files, and extraction failures.
problem: Invoice automation fails in practice when it assumes every email contains a valid, readable invoice with complete fields. Real inboxes contain duplicates, notices that are not invoices, damaged files, scanned PDFs, and incomplete documents.
system: The workflow screens incoming email, identifies invoice candidates, extracts structured fields from email bodies or PDF attachments, validates required information, builds a deduplication key, stores successful or warning-state records, and sends rejected or failed inputs to an explicit error log.

engineeringDecisions.title: Separate candidate detection from extraction
engineeringDecisions.detail: Irrelevant mail and clear non-invoice notices are filtered before expensive extraction work.

engineeringDecisions.title: Keep warning states
engineeringDecisions.detail: An otherwise useful invoice with a missing field can be stored as processed-with-warnings instead of being treated the same as a corrupted document.

engineeringDecisions.title: Persist a stable dedupe key
engineeringDecisions.detail: Duplicate detection is represented directly in stored workflow data rather than relying on human review.

reliability.title: Duplicate handling
reliability.detail: Repeated invoice inputs are logged as duplicates rather than silently inserted twice.

reliability.title: Unreadable-file handling
reliability.detail: Damaged PDFs and files without usable text layers create explicit extraction failures.

reliability.title: Non-invoice handling
reliability.detail: Payment-method reminders and unrelated newsletters are recorded as non-invoice/not-candidate outcomes.

result: A workflow that demonstrates automation reliability through the unhappy paths as clearly as the successful extraction path, with a usable audit trail for every processed email.

evidence.label: Processed invoice register
evidence.description: Evidence includes successful PDF/body extraction and warning states for incomplete fields.

evidence.label: Failure register
evidence.description: Evidence includes duplicate, non-invoice, irrelevant-email, damaged-PDF, and no-text-layer outcomes.

title: Malaria Detection with CNNs
summary: A two-stage computer-vision application that first validates uploaded blood-cell imagery and then classifies valid cells as malaria-infected or uninfected.
problem: A malaria classifier should not confidently classify arbitrary images that are outside its training domain. The application needed a simple guard before the diagnostic model so obvious non-cell inputs would not be treated as blood-smear predictions.
system: Users upload an image through Streamlit. A first classifier checks whether the input is a valid blood-cell image; accepted images are then resized for a CNN that predicts infected or uninfected and returns a confidence score with analysis time.

engineeringDecisions.title: Add an input-domain gate
engineeringDecisions.detail: A separate cell-image classifier rejects obvious non-cell imagery before malaria inference.

engineeringDecisions.title: Deploy the model as an interactive app
engineeringDecisions.detail: Streamlit turns the trained classifiers into a testable end-user workflow rather than leaving them in a notebook.

reliability.title: Explicit invalid-input path
reliability.detail: Non-cell images produce an error state instead of an infected/uninfected prediction.

reliability.title: Confidence and analysis time
reliability.detail: The interface exposes prediction confidence and processing time alongside the class result.

result: An applied-ML project that demonstrates both model inference and a simple but important guardrail around the model’s intended input domain.

evidence.label: Source repository
evidence.description: Streamlit deployment script and trained model artifacts for validation and malaria classification.
